$comment: C 6.4.4.4p7 (D-CSUBSET-NARROW-HEX-ESCAPE-TRUNCATED-TO-TWO-DIGITS): a \x escape consumes EVERY following hex digit. DSS used to cap at two and emit `04 31 00` for "\x041" with rc 0 and no diagnostic, where gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3, mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 and MSVC 19.51 all emit `41 00` (MEASURED 2026-09-02, each compiled and RUN, emitted bytes read back). Every arm here is VALUE-dependent - byte reads plus sizeof - so the two-digit regression flips the exit code instead of passing over a wrong string; stdout carries an independent witness. Modeled on adjacent_string_escape_boundary (4 targets, per-target expectedStdout) + its release shippedPipeline arm.

optimizedPipelines.label: release
optimizedPipelines.$comment: The work this example pins happens entirely in phase 5 of translation - the escape decoder - so the optimizer has nothing of it to transform and the image is expected to be identical to the baseline. Deliberately NOT given mustDifferFromBaseline: an honest no-op, not a missed opt-in. The arm still earns its place by proving the decoded bytes survive the shipped pipeline unchanged.
